SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: 6-week history of generalized body aches, fatigue, reduced energy; feels “run-down.”
  • Onset: ~2 weeks after returning from U.S. holiday (symptom onset late Jan/early Feb 2023).  
  • Course: Persistent; no clear progression.
  • Associated symptoms: mild decrease in appetite (smaller portions, no weight change), occasional nonspecific headache; no cough, SOB, chest pain, sore throat currently, dysphagia, reflux, abdominal pain, bowel or urinary changes, neurological deficits, or joint swelling.
- Rash history: Erythematous circular rash on posterior calf noted mid-/late Feb; minimal itch, faded over ~2 weeks; photo shown. Mild sore throat and possible low-grade fever at that time.
- Past medical history: Asthma, hay fever.
- Medications:
  • Preventive asthma inhaler – drug/dose/route/frequency not documented (patient states daily use AM/PM).  
  • Antihistamine – name/dose/route/frequency not documented (OTC).
- Social history:
  • Occupation: Works for a health technology company.  
  • Lives with wife.  
  • Alcohol: Occasional.  
  • Smoking: Not clearly documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No vitals or physical examination findings recorded during tele-consultation.
- Historical finding: Clinician viewed photograph of resolved circular calf rash (location: posterior calf, side not specified); no current skin lesions.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Fatigue and generalized myalgias
   - Assessment: Non-specific fatigue/myalgia of unclear etiology.
   - Differential diagnosis: Post-viral fatigue, anemia, thyroid disorder, hepatic/renal dysfunction, inflammatory or autoimmune disorder.
   - Investigations planned: Blood tests—CBC, renal profile, liver function tests, thyroid function, inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP).
   - Treatment planned: Pending investigation results.

2. Possible Lyme disease
   - Assessment: Suspected Lyme disease (history of outdoor activity, resolved calf rash compatible with erythema migrans, systemic symptoms).
   - Investigations planned: Borrelia burgdorferi serology.
   - Treatment planned: If serology positive, commence appropriate antibiotic course (drug/dose/route/frequency to be determined based on result and guideline).
   - Follow-up: Arrange telephone review ~1 week after blood tests.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: Allergies, complete smoking history, medication names/doses/routes/frequencies, family history, vitals, systems review for mood/sleep, physical examination.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio dropouts; some patient responses unclear but overall clinically usable.
